stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist has not sought an extension or other relief from the Board. Which continuing education plan satisfies the annual requirements?

choices.text: Five live hours, including one hour of pharmacy law, plus 15 home-study hours with no additional pharmacy-law content
Four live hours, including two hours of pharmacy law, plus 16 home-study hours
Six live hours, including one hour of pharmacy law, plus 14 home-study hours that include one hour of pharmacy law
Nine live hours, including two hours of pharmacy law, plus 10 home-study hours
Three live hours, including two hours of pharmacy law, plus 17 home-study hours

explanation.core_reasoning: The pharmacist must complete 20 continuing education hours each calendar year. At least two hours must concern pharmacy law, and no more than 15 hours may be satisfied through home study or other mediated instruction. Choice C totals 20 hours, uses only 14 home-study hours, and supplies two pharmacy-law hours across the two formats.

choice_analysis.A: The total and home-study cap are satisfied, but the plan contains only one pharmacy-law hour.
choice_analysis.B: The total and pharmacy-law minimum are satisfied, but 16 home-study hours exceed the 15-hour cap.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: 6 plus 14 equals 20, the home-study component is below the cap, and the two pharmacy-law hours satisfy the minimum.
choice_analysis.D: The modality and pharmacy-law requirements are satisfied, but the plan totals only 19 hours.
choice_analysis.E: The total and pharmacy-law minimum are satisfied, but 17 home-study hours exceed the cap.

related_facts: The Board may consider an extenuating-circumstances request through a separate process.
The annual requirements must be tested independently: total hours, instructional format, and pharmacy-law content.
explanation.mpje_trap: A plan can reach 20 total hours and still fail because pharmacy-law content is too low or home study exceeds the separate cap.

reasoning_steps: Add the live and home-study hours
Compare the home-study hours with the 15-hour cap
Confirm that at least two hours concern pharmacy law
